gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '0.01 mm' and '0.125 ms' figures on these $37-$45 boards are not like-for-like: Redragon states only a 0.1 mm adjustment step for the K617 HE (and warns its 0.1-0.2 mm settings are subject to component tolerances) where MCHOSE and Epomaker state 0.01 mm, and the '0.125 ms latency' Redragon and Epomaker print is one 8,000 Hz report interval (1 s / 8,000), not a measured delay.
standout_why: Compared against the four rival pages I could read. mechanicalkeyboard.net (dated 2026-11-10) gives no rapid-trigger step, dead zone or scan rate for any board; it does say 8,000 Hz means one report per 0.125 ms and is not total input delay, so it has the latency half in general terms but does not tie it to the makers' '0.125 ms latency' lines. setupinsider.com gives no step for the K617 HE. gamepadsquire.com gives 0.01 mm and 128 kHz for the HE68 Lite and only the 0.1-3.4 mm actuation range for a Redragon board, with no step comparison. keyboardverdict.com covers none of these boards' steps. None quotes Redragon's tolerance caveat or puts the 0.1 mm and 0.01 mm figures side by side; ChatGPT's own answer lists the K617 HE with 'adjustable actuation' and no step. Not a 3 because the two CITED pages (PC Gamer best Hall effect, RTINGS rapid trigger research) returned only navigation to my fetches, so I could not check them, and RTINGS' title ('...But Any Of Them Will Do') argues that step differences rarely decide anything.
decides: It splits ChatGPT's four near-identical sub-$45 picks. On maker-stated figures the Redragon K617 HE ($39.99) is the coarsest (0.1 mm step, maker's own tolerance warning at 0.1-0.2 mm, no scan rate stated), so it drops out of 'spend as little as possible'. The 0.01 mm boards are then separated by price and layout, not by the latency lines, which are polling arithmetic or unverified maker claims: Gamakay NS68 wired $36.79 (65%, arrow keys), MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro from $37.40 (60%), Epomaker HE68 Lite $42.49 (65%). That supports the NS68 placing in the top three on price among the sellers read today, provided its 0.01 mm and 8K figures are confirmed on Gamakay's page body, which I could not open (HTTP 429); only the product title carries them. Caveat for the page: every latency figure here is a maker claim, none measured.
